debug.title: The Lock That Never Let Go
debug.description: A worker thread deposits amount a, then main deposits amount b, both guarded by one lock. A non-positive amount is rejected with an exception. After a rejected deposit the next deposit wrongly times out. Input: two integers a and b. Output: any 'rejected' or 'timeout' lines, then 'Balance: ' and the total.
hints: Try the input -1 7. The second deposit should succeed, but it says timeout. Who still owns the lock?
Trace deposit(-1): which lines run before the exception is thrown, and which line never runs?
The exception skips lock.unlock(), so the dead worker thread keeps the lock forever and main can never acquire it.
Wrap the guarded work in try { ... } finally { lock.unlock(); } so the lock is released on every path.
